title: Role contracts, with vendors as data
subtitle: Work is assigned to a role with a contract; which model fills the seat is configuration, and reviewers can be a different vendor from builders on purpose
lede: Every model vendor would like to be the system. I treat them as workers. A job in my platform is addressed to a role with a contract: what it receives, what it must return, what it may touch, how much it may spend. Which model fills that seat, at what reasoning effort, under which account, is per-seat data. The same role can be filled by a frontier model through its subscription command-line tool, by an API seat, by a local open-source model on my own GPUs, or by a swarm job, and the contract does not change. A role contract names inputs, outputs, tool classes and budget.
quote: The contract is the product and the vendor is a supplier.
evidence: Model-agnostic agent architecture: jobs addressed to role contracts naming inputs, outputs, tool classes and budget, with model, reasoning effort and account as per-seat data.
Separation of duties for AI work: builders on one model family and quality and adversarial reviewers on another, so their blind spots do not overlap.
Agent orchestration: subscription command-line tools, API seats, local open-source models and swarm jobs filling the same role, behind a terms-of-service firewall.
author: Corey James
